focus: Company B, 25th Aviation Battalion (mid-1966 through mid-1967)

units.name: 25th Aviation Battalion
units.description: Company B, 25th Aviation Battalion served in Vietnam from mid-1966 through mid-1967. The unit operated in the Cu Chi and Iron Triangle region, conducting support and transport operations. Multiple pilots from Company B earned Air Medals for their service during this period.

notable_personnel.name: Arthur P. Lancy Jr.
notable_personnel.award_source: Tropic Lightning News, Vol. 2 No. 13, April 3, 1967

training_classes.significance: Class 65-9W was among the first full classes to utilize the Hughes TH-55A Osage as the Army's primary trainer at Fort Wolters. This class represents the 'dawn of the Osage era' in Army Aviation training.

hughes_th55a_adoption.significance: Marked a major transition in Army Aviation primary training from fixed-wing to rotary-wing aircraft
hughes_th55a_adoption.class_65_9w_role: Among the first full classes to train on the Osage at Fort Wolters

tropic_lightning_news.entry: WO Arthur P. Lancy, Co. B, 25th Avn. Bn.

FW-ARC-0001.training_significance: Named recipient of presentation lighter commemorating first graduating class using Hughes TH-55A Osage
FW-ARC-0001.service_significance: Recipient later earned Air Medal in Co. B, 25th Avn. Bn., Vietnam

research_notes.scope: This archive focuses exclusively on Company B, 25th Aviation Battalion during its service period of mid-1966 through mid-1967.
research_notes.primary_artifact: The Class 65-9WA presentation lighter named to WOC Arthur P. Lancy Jr. serves as the centerpiece artifact connecting Fort Wolters training to Vietnam service.
research_notes.data_integrity: All claims are tied to verified external sources (VHPA, Tropic Lightning News, 25th Infantry Division Association).
research_notes.limitations: The Tropic Lightning News citation establishes later service context only and does not prove the lighter was carried or used during Vietnam service.
